senses.definition: A movement, sound, or light used to send a message, instruction, or warning to people.

examples.en: The referee blew his whistle as a signal to start the match.
examples.vi: Trọng tài thổi còi như một tín hiệu để bắt đầu trận đấu.

senses.definition: Radio waves or electrical currents carrying sounds, images, or data to electronic devices.

examples.en: I could not make a call because there was no phone signal.
examples.vi: Tôi không thể gọi điện vì không có sóng điện thoại.

senses.definition: An event or action that clearly indicates what is happening or might happen soon.

examples.en: The increase in sales is a clear signal of business recovery.
examples.vi: Sự gia tăng doanh số là một dấu hiệu rõ ràng của việc kinh doanh phục hồi.

thesaurus.definition: any nonverbal action or gesture that encodes a message
any incitement to action
an electric quantity (voltage or current or field strength) whose modulation represents coded information about the source from which it comes

vi_block: Dấu hiệu, tín hiệu; hiệu lệnh.

wiktionary.gloss: A sequence of states representing an encoded message in a communication channel.
Any variation of a quantity or change in an entity over time that conveys information upon detection.
A sign made to give notice of some occurrence, command, or danger, or to indicate the start of a concerted action.
An on-off light, semaphore, or other device used to give an indication to another person.
A railway signal.

examples: My mobile phone can't get a signal in the railway station.
wiktionary.gloss: An electromagnetic action, normally a voltage that is a function of time, that conveys the information of the radio or TV program or of communication with another party.
An action, change or process done to convey information and thus reduce uncertainty.
A token; an indication; a foreshadowing; a sign.
Useful information, as opposed to noise.
A simple interprocess communication used to notify a process or thread of an occurrence.
A signalling interaction between cells

blocks.etymology: From Old French segnal, seignal or Medieval Latin signāle; noun use of the neuter of Late Latin signālis, from Latin signum; verb use from 1805, as a shortened from signalize (1650s). Doublet of signum and sign.

senses.definition: To communicate information or make your intentions known through a movement, sound, or sign.

examples.en: He raised his right hand to signal the car to stop.
examples.vi: Anh ấy giơ tay phải lên để ra hiệu cho chiếc xe dừng lại.

senses.definition: To be a sign that a specific action, change, or event will take place.

examples.en: The minister's speech signals a major change in government education policy.
examples.vi: Bài phát biểu của bộ trưởng báo hiệu một sự thay đổi lớn trong chính sách giáo dục của chính phủ.

thesaurus.definition: communicate silently and non-verbally by signals or signs
be a signal for or a symptom of

vi_block: Ra hiệu, báo hiệu; chuyển (tin tức, lệnh) bằng tín hiệu.

examples: I signalled my acquiescence with a nod.
He whistled to signal that we should stop.
wiktionary.gloss: To indicate; to convey or communicate by a signal.

examples: Seeing the flames, he ran to the control room and signalled headquarters.
wiktionary.gloss: To communicate with (a person or system) by a signal.

blocks.etymology: From Old French segnal, seignal or Medieval Latin signāle; noun use of the neuter of Late Latin signālis, from Latin signum; verb use from 1805, as a shortened from signalize (1650s). Doublet of signum and sign.

senses.definition: Very important, remarkable, or noticeable.

examples.en: The historic peace agreement was celebrated as a signal victory for diplomacy.
examples.vi: Thỏa thuận hòa bình lịch sử được tán dương như một thắng lợi nổi bật của nền ngoại giao.

senses.vi: đáng chú ý; nổi bật; đáng kể

vi_block: Đáng kể, đáng chú ý, nổi tiếng; gương mẫu; nghiêm minh.
Dùng làm dấu hiệu, để ra hiệu.

examples: a signal exploit; a signal success; a signal act of benevolence
wiktionary.gloss: Standing above others in rank, importance, or achievement.

idioms.gloss: To practice virtue signalling.
to share or disseminate another's information or material with one's own audience

blocks.etymology: From Middle English unfolden, from Old English unfealdan (“to unfold”), equivalent to un- + fold.

senses.definition: to open something that was folded, or to become open in this way

examples.en: He unfolded the map on the table.
examples.vi: Anh ấy mở tấm bản đồ ra trên bàn.

examples.en: The flower petals slowly unfolded in the sun.
examples.vi: Những cánh hoa từ từ mở ra dưới ánh mặt trời.

senses.definition: to happen or develop over time as a story or situation progresses

examples.en: We watched the dramatic events unfold on live television.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi theo dõi các sự kiện kịch tính diễn ra trên truyền hình trực tiếp.

senses.definition: to make a plan, secret, or story known to other people gradually

examples.en: The manager unfolded his strategy to the team.
examples.vi: Người quản lý đã bộc lộ chiến lược của mình với cả đội.

senses.vi: bộc lộ; bày tỏ; để lộ

thesaurus.definition: develop or come to a promising stage
open to the view
extend or stretch out to a greater or the full length
spread out or open from a closed or folded state

wiktionary.gloss: To turn out; to happen; to develop.
